formattedAddress: No. 376號, Changchun Rd, 中山區 Zhongshan District, Taipei City, Taiwan 10491

text.text:
This is our first time at Sapori.  My tween daughter loves pasta so we decided to try this restaurant having had lots of Taiwanese and Japanese food eat outs already.

The ambience is cozy, the walls are decorated with lots of distinctions and awards won by the Chef.  The restaurant manager is courteous, friendly and efficient and can speak Mandarin, Taiwanese, English and even Filipino!

We ordered the octopus leg for our appetizer and it tasted great, with just the right amount of charring.  For our main course, we shared a plate/bowl of lasagna which was very unique tasting and quite different from the mass-produced ones at grocery stores or fast food chains.  For dessert, we had the apple pie/crumble which was also unique and scrumptious.

I’m not going to pretend we are connoisseurs but we really enjoyed the food, the hospitality and the location really wasn’t that bad, maybe a 10 minute walk from the Nanjing Fuxing subway station.

Would definitely recommend this place to anyone who’s willing to try authentic Italian meal, prepared by an award-winning Chef.  The Manager confirmed that food is prepared fresh daily and that only quality ingredients and passion go into each dish.  Definitely call in the book a reservation, seating is limited and the restaurant is only open evenings, Wednesday to Sunday.

text.text: Handmade pasta, soulful sauces, and desserts that look like art but taste even better. You can tell the chef cooks with passion, not just skill. Every visit feels special, like dining at a friend’s home who happens to be an incredible Italian chef.

text.text: A tiny corner of Taipei that feels like a trattoria hidden in Florence. The food bursts with authentic flavor, rich sauces, and perfect textures. Everything tastes fresh and honest, the kind of meal that makes you want to linger a little longer.
